metadata.title: Inspect a zone and a supplied validation finding
metadata.topic: DNS Operations — Offline Evidence (Simulator / Offline snapshots)

mission.brief: Read zone identity, records and a concrete CNAME conflict without pretending to validate or reload it. Retain the first seven records: context, origin, SOA, NS, both portal records and validation. Omit the unrelated host. Save the required factual records in report.txt and display the final report with cat. Self-review the interpretation and next checks in HELP.txt.
constraints: SIMULATOR / OFFLINE SNAPSHOTS: fictional supplied evidence, not live measurements of your computer or VM. Read reference.txt for source excerpts and HELP.txt for context/model interpretation.
Automatic score checks exact factual report bytes (80) and final cat report.txt (20). Free-form reasoning, diagnoses and next checks are self-reviewed; 100/100 is not mastery.

Keep record spelling, order and final LF exactly; equivalent supported paths/filters are accepted, arbitrary report formatting is not normalized. Only report.txt is writable. > truncates first; failures do not undo writes. Finish all writes before the checked reading; any write clears prior reading evidence.

Challenge states the same factual requirements without a repair command. No service changes, live lookups, certificate validation, shell or network execution. Type help for supported commands; cat HELP.txt for this lesson reference.

hints: Compare the question with the supplied vantage points, timestamps and fields. What conflict is actually reported, and what intended-design information is missing?

Read reference.txt and HELP.txt. The portal owner has both CNAME and A data, which is not permitted for these ordinary records. Decide which intended record should exist before proposing a correction. This supplied validator finding does not assess intended addresses, delegation, running server configuration or a successful reload. Serial is a zone version, not automatically a timestamp or proof of publication. Select only the required records; do not add a causal conclusion to the scored factual report.
A supported construction is: head -n 7 evidence.txt > report.txt. Then cat report.txt. Interpret the result separately; this score checks facts and inspection only.

/home/learner/HELP.txt.content:
SIMULATOR / OFFLINE SNAPSHOTS — Inspect a zone and a supplied validation finding
Goal: Read zone identity, records and a concrete CNAME conflict without pretending to validate or reload it.
These original synthetic annotated records describe fictional hosts, not your computer or a VM. reference.txt gives realistic source excerpts; evidence.txt contains normalized records for extraction, not literal tool output. No ip, ping, ss, dig, named-checkzone, curl, openssl, Apache or nginx command executes here.
Task: Retain the first seven records: context, origin, SOA, NS, both portal records and validation. Omit the unrelated host.
Report format: preserve the selected record spelling, order and final LF exactly. Equivalent supported filters and paths are accepted; alternative prose/formatting is not normalized. Only report.txt is writable. Finish every write before cat report.txt; a later write invalidates reading evidence. Type help for the bounded text-command syntax.
Automatically checked: report facts (80 points) and displaying that final report with cat (20 points). No points for reading every source. A 100/100 score is NOT verified diagnostic reasoning or operational mastery.
Self-review questions: What conflict is actually reported, and what intended-design information is missing?
Model interpretation: The portal owner has both CNAME and A data, which is not permitted for these ordinary records. Decide which intended record should exist before proposing a correction. This supplied validator finding does not assess intended addresses, delegation, running server configuration or a successful reload. Serial is a zone version, not automatically a timestamp or proof of publication.
Common mistakes: Treating a CNAME target as another address; removing an arbitrary record without requirements; assuming a serial or successful syntax check proves live service correctness.
Reasoning, proposed next checks and causal claims are self-reviewed, not keyword graded. Challenge hides guided commands and hints; this conceptual reference remains available.
Reset restores sources/reports and starts a new attempt, preserving history. Resume retains report, pending input, mode and exact scenario identity. This complements real practice; no live configuration or network effect occurs.
